notes: v10 = v9 with one universe change (2026-11-24 06:30 UTC review): a token can be traded from 3 days after launch, was 1 day (universe.min_age_days 1 to 3). A risk limit, not a claim about returns. Why: the test written on 17 Nov at 14:30, when the floor went to 1 day, was met. It said the floor goes to 3 days if one day's trades on tokens 1 to 3 days old cost more than 5% of equity. On 24 Nov the one such trade, UCASH (7cFiq..., 1.62 days, a pumpswap pool of $99k), lost 0.3526 SOL, 8.8% of the day's starting equity (4.0150 SOL): its price fell 85% and its pool 62% in one on-time five-minute cycle (03:15 to 03:20) 70 minutes after the buy, so no stop could act. The count branch of the same test was not yet reached but points the same way: 12 band trades since 16 Nov, 4 winners, -10.63% a trade, against +0.21% on 26 trades on older tokens over the same days (-4.76% without UCASH). In v9 the 7 band trades made -18.03% a trade, the 17 older +2.81%. The replay with the 3-day floor (in-sample, a hint) closes 36 trades at +1.94% against 51 at -1.39%. It costs entries: over the last 24 hours 9 of 25 tokens that passed the universe, and 21% of universe readings, were 1 to 3 days old. What the floor blocks stays measurable: python3 -m bot.replay --set universe.min_age_days=1. v9 = v8 with one universe change (2026-11-19 06:30 UTC review): a token whose 24-hour volume is more than 150 times its pool is outside the universe (new key universe.max_volume_h24_to_liquidity, 150). A tightening, and a risk limit, not a claim about returns. Why: the test written on 17 Nov at 22:30 was met. It said to add this cap if a second token with volume over 100 times its pool passed the universe for an hour or more. The first was ANT (address ELR9i...) on 17 Nov: $47M a day through a $125k pool, inside the universe for 58 cycles, then the pool read $0 in one cycle. The second is another ANT (8J2VU...) on 19 Nov: $43M to $48M a day through a pool of $123k to $155k (278 to 386 times), inside the universe on 64 cycles in a row from 01:20 UTC and still there at the review. Both were kept from a buy only by buy pressure of 1.06 to 1.11 against the 1.2 needed, a test not written for this; a buy would have lost the whole position, about 10% of equity. Why 150 and not the 100 named on 17 Nov: that entry said 100 unless the data showed a tradable token above it, and it does (inuhao up to 116 and FOOD up to 107 on 13 and 14 Nov; a buy at any of their 77 cycles above 100 made +10.2% on average). Nothing on the record sits between 116 and 278, so any number from 120 to 270 gives the same record; 150 is a judgment. The cap changes no trade the bot ever made (the highest at any real entry is 40) and no replayed trade, so v8's open tests carry on unchanged across v8 and v9. Measure what it blocks with: python3 -m bot.replay --set universe.max_volume_h24_to_liquidity=1000000. v8 = v7 with one universe change (2026-11-17 14:30 UTC review): a token can be traded from 1 day after launch, was 3 hours (universe.min_age_days 0.125 to 1). Why: the test written on 16 Nov, when the 3-hour floor went in at Ajeeb's request, was met. It said to raise the floor, to 1 day first, if one day's trades on young tokens cost more than 5% of equity. On 17 Nov the four trades on tokens under a day old (GTA, LEOSTAR, BAWSAQ, bul; 9 to 16 hours old) cost 0.2523 SOL, 5.6% of the day's starting equity. Two of their three stops filled at -28% and -24% on price against a 12% level with every cycle on time, BAWSAQ was 88% under the buy price 30 minutes after the buy, and LEOSTAR fell 78% in one cycle ten minutes after the bot sold it. On the recorded snapshots the entry rules' first signals on tokens under a day old made -20.9% (13 on 8 tokens, 6 of them worse than -25%) against +4.6% at 1 to 3 days (11 on 4 tokens) and +4.4% at 3 days or more (29 on 8). Hints, on one bad day and few tokens; it is a risk limit, not a claim about returns. Tokens 1 to 3 days old stay tradable and are still judged apart. What the floor blocks stays measurable: python3 -m bot.replay --set universe.min_age_days=0.125. v7 = v6 with exit.trailing_stop_pct 10 to 5 (2026-11-16 22:30 UTC review: with one price every 5 minutes the half kept after the first target was sold far under a 10% trail level). v6 = v5 with universe.min_age_days 3 to 0.125, at Ajeeb's request on 2026-11-16 (his hypothesis: the volume in young tokens is genuine). v5 = v4 with entry.min_txns_h1 150 to 300 (2026-11-16 06:30 UTC review; a signal on a thinly traded token has been reliably bad).
